messages.text: Sunday, November 15 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies, clarinet recitals, and the quiet drift of herbicide

A cool, grey Saturday in Canton brings a focus on musical performance and local environmental research. We look at the subtle ways chemicals reshape our fields and how regional management is changing the way we live alongside deer.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 44 degrees and a low around 31 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:25 AM and sets at 5:12 PM, with the moon currently in a waxing crescent phase at 29.3 percent illumination.
Musical afternoons in Ann Arbor
Graduate student Jaden Tan performs a clarinet recital at 2 PM at the Earl V. Moore Building, followed by the Student Composer Concert Series at 7 PM in the same venue.
A community meeting is scheduled for November 18 at 6:30 PM.
Regional shifts in deer management

Southern Michigan communities are increasingly moving toward regional management strategies to mitigate deer-related traffic accidents and protect local biodiversity. These collaborative efforts aim to address population growth through shared resources rather than isolated municipal actions.

Monday, November 16 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies meet the precision of a tuba recital in Ann Arbor

Sunday brings steady, cool temperatures and a quiet rhythm to our local corner of Michigan. We look toward the intersection of academic inquiry in Ann Arbor and the evolving regional strategies for managing our natural surroundings.
Conditions remain overcast throughout the day with a high near 51 degrees and a low around 36 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:26 AM and sets at 5:11 PM, with the moon in its first quarter phase at 38.3 percent illumination.
Intellectual and musical pursuits

Graduate student Jake Alford performs a free tuba recital at the Walgreen Drama Center in Ann Arbor at 8 PM. Earlier in the afternoon, East Hall hosts a seminar on the algebra of foliations at 3 PM and a lecture on Hurwitz spaces at 4 PM.
A meeting is scheduled for November 18 at 6:30 PM.
Regional deer management and local legal shifts

Southern Michigan communities are increasingly forming regional coalitions to manage growing deer populations and improve traffic safety. Meanwhile, a defamation lawsuit has been filed in Wayne County Circuit Court by the publisher of Michigan's Arab American News against former U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
